analysis.title: Softer Jobs Data Gives Fed Room to Pause
key_insights: September payroll growth came in below expectations and the prior two months were revised down, but labor-force participation rose and the workweek stabilized instead of falling as expected.
Manufacturing employment has added roughly 70,000 to 75,000 jobs since the start of the year.
The unemployment rate rose one-tenth, while the broader U6 underemployment rate fell one-tenth. Siegel reads this as a labor market cooling, not breaking.

Siegel argues the Fed has good reason to pause in October because wage pressure is modest, oil has stabilized and the jobs data are ambiguous. It could still move more aggressively in December if inflation forces it.
Taking an October hike off the table removes one of the market's main near-term concerns.
WTI appears to be settling into a roughly $90 to $100 range, and the economy has handled higher energy prices without visible deterioration.

The 30-year TIPS yield recently reached nearly 3.4%. With the market near 20 times earnings (about a 5% earnings yield), the equity risk premium is only about 1.6 percentage points, which Siegel expects to matter increasingly for allocation.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq remain within reach of new highs despite the rise in real yields. Siegel reads this as evidence that earnings and growth expectations remain very strong.
The AI capital-spending cycle continues, with no meaningful slowdown yet, and fourth-quarter earnings should be very strong year over year.

Higher rates pressure value companies more than large technology and growth firms. A hyperscaler with 40% to 60% operating margins absorbs an extra point of financing cost more easily than a company with 8% to 10% margins.
The earlier broadening toward value has reversed and technology and growth have regained relative strength. Siegel expects that to persist while real rates stay elevated.
Siegel remains constructive on equities: high real rates tighten valuations, but strong earnings expectations in technology and AI are outweighing that headwind.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscalers with 40-60% operating margins absorb higher financing costs better, and AI capex and earnings expectations remain strong.
Companies with 8-10% margins are more exposed to higher rates, and the earlier rotation toward value has reversed.

earnings_insights: Siegel expects fourth-quarter earnings to be very strong on a year-over-year basis, with no figure given.
The market trades near 20 times earnings, implying roughly a 5% earnings yield.
